title: Face and common brick palette for the K03 walls: the period bricks a house's front and its side and rear walls are laid in, each as a tint over a K03 panel 1904 already loads
reader: generators/archetypes/k03_brick.py (recipe), read for a K01 record's `face_brick` by generators/archetypes/k01_frontage_params.py
owner: 2026-11-05: "this is prairie avenue and they would have nice face brick and it would be different for houses ... use that base model and probably add more versions with tuned color and material based on the correct time period and likely brick styles across all the buildings"
rule: Every recipe is the K03 panel it names, unchanged (its bricks, its joints, its bond, and the renderer's per-brick shuffle, brick-bond.js), under a colour factor and a roughness shift. The factor is mean_linear over the panel's own mean (material.json mean_srgb, linearised) and must lie in [0, 1] on each channel, so a recipe only ever darkens or re-hues a panel and never asks a glTF base colour factor over 1. No recipe adds a map: 1904 is at its phone memory ceiling, and both panels named here are already loaded there. A face recipe goes on the street front (and its brick bays); a common recipe on the side and rear walls, the stacks and the area walls. Which recipe a house wears is the record's (`face_brick`), read off its own pictures where it has them.

pressed_red.name: Pressed red front brick
pressed_red.note: Dry-pressed red face brick, the eastern ('Philadelphia' or 'Baltimore') front brick and its western makers' copies, the fashionable front of the 1870s and early 1880s: a smooth, even red face with sharp arrises in a thin joint, its mortar stained to the brick so the front reads as one colour field. Laid over the common panel, whose lime joints the factor stains with the brick.

pressed_red_deep.name: Deep red pressed brick
pressed_red_deep.note: A darker, bluer red pressed brick, the dark reds the large hydraulic-press works sold from the 1880s; in running bond, the face laid without headers.

red_brown.name: Rough red-brown brick
red_brown.note: The library's rough red-brown brick in light joints, unchanged: the brick T-3244 read off 1700-1708 Prairie's photographs.

pressed_brown.name: Brown pressed brick
pressed_brown.note: A dark brown pressed brick of the Queen Anne and Romanesque 1880s fronts, laid to read nearly as dark as brownstone.

pressed_buff.name: Buff pressed brick
pressed_buff.note: A clean golden-buff pressed brick (the Ohio and Indiana fire-clay buffs of the 1890s), smoother and warmer than the city's common buff.

cream_sooted.name: Cream front brick, smoke-dulled
cream_sooted.note: A pale cream front brick of the 1850s and 1860s (Milwaukee's lake-clay 'cream city' brick was shipped to Chicago), its porous face greyed by thirty and more years of the city's soft-coal smoke by 1904: the common panel's own body, a shade duller in its red. The library has no paler panel than the common buff, so a fresh cream is not laid.

common_buff.name: Chicago common brick, buff
common_buff.note: The K03 common panel as it is: the local lake clay, high in lime, fired buff to salmon in scove kilns; the brick of side, party and rear walls.

common_salmon.name: Chicago common brick, salmon
common_salmon.note: The same common burnt pinker: a salmon kiln run.

common_yellow.name: Chicago common brick, yellow
common_yellow.note: The same common burnt yellower: a buff-yellow kiln run.

common_dun.name: Chicago common brick, smoke-dulled
common_dun.note: The common buff dulled by the city's smoke on an older or north-facing flank.
